```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

Each MFRI stock repo keeps three history tables in `data/`, which the advice
sheets and tech reports read:

* `data/assessment.csv`: the assessment summary, one row per year and
  assessment year (the columns of `hafroreports::hr_assessment_template()`);
* `data/advice_hist.csv`: the advice for each fishing year;
* `data/tac_hist.csv`: the TAC, entered by hand after it is set.

For a category 3 stock, dlsrules makes this assessment's rows:
`assessment_summary()` for the summary and `advice_hist_rows()` for the
advice. `rfb_ref_points_table()` gives the reference point table. The
category 3 stocks that use them are listed in `vignette("rfb-rule")` and
`vignette("chr-rule")`; 25-wit is the simplest example.

```{r}
library(dlsrules)
```

## Simulated inputs

```{r}
set.seed(1)
years <- 1985:2025
b <- round(2000 * exp(cumsum(c(0, rnorm(length(years) - 1, 0, 0.15)))))
survey_index <- rbind(
  data.frame(index = "smb_harv", year = years, b = b,
             b_cv = round(runif(length(years), 0.12, 0.3), 2),
             n = round(b / 0.6), n_cv = 0.2),
  data.frame(index = "smb_rec", year = years, b = round(b / 5), b_cv = 0.3,
             n = round(rlnorm(length(years), log(1500), 0.4)),
             n_cv = round(runif(length(years), 0.2, 0.4), 2))
)

z <- 0.12 + 0.05 * sin(seq_along(1990:2024) / 4)
ldist <- expand.grid(length = 20:70, year = 1990:2024)
ldist$n <- round(
  2000 * plogis((ldist$length - 32) / 1.5) *
    exp(-z[ldist$year - 1989] * (ldist$length - 32) / 1.2 * (ldist$length > 32))
)
ldist <- ldist[, c("year", "length", "n")]

assessment_year <- 2025
ref_points <- ref_points_iloss(
  list(K = 0.147, Linf = 62.1, Lc = 33, F_msy_proxy = 1),
  index_series(survey_index, "smb_harv", year_end = assessment_year),
  method = "min"
)
prognosis <- rfb_advice(
  index_series(survey_index, "smb_harv"), ldist, ref_points,
  prev_tac = 1659, assessment_year = assessment_year
)
```

## Assessment summary

For a category 3 stock the summary shows the biomass index as SSB, a
recruitment index (abundance), and a fishing pressure measure as F or HR,
each with 95% intervals where it has a CV.

For an rfb stock F is the fishing pressure proxy L~F=M~ / L~mean~
(F~MSY~ proxy = 1). `fproxy_series()` gives it by year; the years are
arguments, because they change the table:

```{r}
fp <- fproxy_series(
  ldist,
  Lc = ref_points$Lc,
  Linf = ref_points$Linf,
  year_start = -Inf,
  year_end = assessment_year - 1
)
tail(fp, 3)

rows <- assessment_summary(
  survey_index,
  ssb_index = "smb_harv",
  rec_index = "smb_rec",
  fishing_pressure = fp,
  species = 25,
  assessment_year = assessment_year,
  ssb_ci = "lognormal",
  rec_ci = "lognormal"
)
tail(rows, 3)
```

The last year has no F: the catch sampling of the assessment year is not
complete. For a chr stock (04-whg), pass `landings` instead of (or as well
as) `fishing_pressure`: landings / SSB index is shown as `median_HR` up to
`landings_year_end` (default the year before the assessment year).

```{r}
landings <- data.frame(year = 1985:2024, landings = round(b[1:40] * 0.25))
tail(assessment_summary(
  survey_index, ssb_index = "smb_harv", rec_index = NULL,
  landings = landings, species = 4, assessment_year = assessment_year,
  ssb_ci = "normal"
), 3)
```

The intervals are log-normal, x exp(∓1.96 CV), unless `"normal"` is asked
for, x (1 ∓ 1.96 CV), which can go below zero for a CV above 0.51. 04-whg keeps
the normal interval for its SSB index, as its old code; the other stocks
use log-normal.

## Advice history rows

```{r}
advice_hist_rows(prognosis, assessment_year)
advice_hist_rows(prognosis, assessment_year, n_years = 2)
```

The advice is rounded to whole tonnes. With `n_years = 2` (biennial advice,
see `vignette("stock-choices")`) the same advice is entered for two fishing
years. `basis_en` and `basis_is` set the basis column (04-whg: "CHR rule" /
"CHR reglan").

## Reference point table

```{r}
rfb_ref_points_table(ref_points)
```

I~loss~ (`I_lim`) and I~trigger~ are rounded to whole units of the index
(tonnes). `trl` is L~F=M~.

## Keep the published rows

The history files hold what was published, and a rerun must not change it.
A run on later data gives a slightly different advice for an assessment year
that is already published (a rerun of the cod assessment gave 201,355 t
instead of the published 201,674 t). Each stock repo therefore has
`R/hist.R` with `update_hist(hist, new, template = NULL)`, built on
`hafroreports::hr_update_hist()`. It adds the run's rows only for assessment
years that are not in the file yet. Placeholder rows, with every value
`NA` (e.g. `2026,5a,NA` in `tac_hist.csv` before the TAC is set), are not
published, and the run's rows replace them.

The rule on plain data frames, without hafroreports:

```{r}
keep_published <- function(hist, new) {
  values <- setdiff(names(hist)[vapply(hist, is.numeric, logical(1))],
                    "assessment_year")
  placeholder <- rowSums(!is.na(hist[values])) == 0
  hist <- hist[!(placeholder & hist$assessment_year %in% new$assessment_year), ]
  new <- new[!new$assessment_year %in% hist$assessment_year, ]
  out <- rbind(hist, new)
  out <- out[order(out$assessment_year), ]
  rownames(out) <- NULL
  out
}

published <- data.frame(
  assessment_year = 2023:2024,
  advice_period = c("2023/2024", "2024/2025"),
  advice = c(1500, 1659),
  advice_basis.en = "Domestic advice",
  advice_basis.is = "Innlend ráðgjöf"
)
# A rerun of 2024 on today's data would give another number; the file keeps
# the published 1659 t and only 2025 is added
rerun <- rbind(
  transform(advice_hist_rows(prognosis, 2024), advice = 1702),
  advice_hist_rows(prognosis, 2025)
)
keep_published(published, rerun)
```

In the targets pipeline:

```r
tar_target(
  advice_hist,
  update_hist(
    historical_advice_file,
    dlsrules::advice_hist_rows(rfb_prognosis, assessment_year,
                               n_years = advice_n_years)
  )
),
tar_target(
  assessment_hist,
  update_hist(
    template = hr_assessment_template(),
    historical_assessment_file,
    assessment_rows
  )
)
```

## Pitfalls

* **The files are read, not written.** The targets add this assessment's
  rows in memory. After the advice is published, add the published rows to
  `data/*.csv` by hand, and check that the latest assessment's row is there.
* **Header-only CSV files** (e.g. `tac_hist.csv` of a stock without a TAC)
  read as character columns. Give `readr::read_csv()` the column types.
* **Template by name:** pass `template = hr_assessment_template()` by name;
  `update_hist()`'s first argument is the history.
* **The F proxy years** (`fproxy_series(year_start, year_end)`) and the
  index of the SSB column change the history table and are fixed in the
  stock's `config.R` (`vignette("stock-choices")`).
